lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Eh? Speak up. Thirty years of powder charges took most of my hearing and all of my patience.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Retired miner. Which means I'm the only man in Hollowmere who's been down and come back more times than he can count.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Advice? Aye. Count your rungs going down, and count them again coming up. If the numbers disagree, believe the second one and climb faster.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: And if the dark feels like it's leaning on you — that's not the dark. The dark doesn't lean. Move.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: The Foreman's down, I hear. Hollis. He was a green lad when I last worked beside him, and now he's a story.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: I'll tell you the thing I haven't told the mayor, because she'd worry. I've seen the mine do this before.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: The spring the chapel bell cracked. We lost nine, sealed the level, and the town agreed it was gas. Towns agree to things.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: It wasn't gas. I helped brick that door myself, and the bricks I laid went back in my dreams for twenty years, wet on the outside and dry within. Whatever it is, it's been patient longer than I've been old.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: You've reached the fifth level. Nobody who worked the survey with me believed the fifth went anywhere. Looks like the survey was the optimist.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: There's a door down there the charts call a pump room. It isn't. Check the hinges from the outside and keep it that way.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Brannoc's crew walking back up. I know those lanterns. I saw the same light the spring the bell cracked, and I told myself it was glowworm.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Don't stand between them and the town, and don't let them stand behind you. I've buried enough friends who got those two rules in the wrong order.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: I caught myself talking in my sleep in the old surveyors' code. Haven't used that since the fifth level closed.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: I've started leaving my boots by the door at night, pointed at the mine. Silly habit. I'd like to say I don't know who I'm warning off.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: The mine's gone quiet the way a held breath goes quiet. I've heard it twice in my life. I didn't like it the first time either.

lines.speaker: Old Tom
lines.text: Still breathing? Good. Sit down before you fall down.
